transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Turn off the washing machine at its controls immediately. Do not attempt to unplug it if there is water near the plug or your hands are wet; instead, go to your consumer unit (fuse box) and switch off the circuit that powers the kitchen or specifically the washing machine. Once the power is isolated, do not use the appliance again until a qualified engineer has inspected it. Water reaching an electrical socket under the units creates a risk of electric shock or short-circuiting that cannot be safely resolved by the homeowner. The leak could be from a loose drain hose, a failed pump seal, or a cracked tub, but given the water location near the plug, professional assessment is essential for safety.
I'm standing in socks on the wet floor right now, should I get out of it first? The consumer unit is in the hall and the floor's dry there, so I can get to it.

Yes, please get out of the water immediately and dry your feet before moving to the hall. Once you are safely across the dry floor, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit as planned. Because the water has reached the plug area under the units, this is a serious electrical hazard.
ok I'm out of the water and drying my feet now. I'll go to the hall and switch it off at the fuse box. What do I do after that?

Once you have switched off the power at the consumer unit, please do not touch the machine or try to move it. The water has reached the plug area under the units, which creates a serious risk of electric shock or short-circuiting that cannot be safely resolved by a homeowner. You will need to call a qualified appliance engineer to investigate the leak and ensure the electrical installation is safe before the machine can be used again.
